reference_findings.diagnosis: Suspected no-reflow phenomenon in the educational simulation; exclude mechanical obstruction, dissection, residual lesion and other causes by expert review.
reference_findings.risk_assessment: Severe procedural complication; qualitative simulation label only, not a validated score.

investigation_reports.ecg: Persistent ST elevation/ischemic changes after simulated epicardial opening.
investigation_reports.laboratory_panel: Troponin trend expected to rise in the infarction context; no single biomarker can diagnose no-reflow. Hemoglobin, renal function and electrolytes reviewed for safety.
investigation_reports.echocardiography: New or persistent regional wall-motion abnormality; LVEF estimate 40% in the fictional branch.
investigation_reports.coronary_or_other_imaging: Simulation report: epicardial vessel is patent after the intervention branch but distal myocardial blush/perfusion is poor; flow grade and image quality must be clearly marked as synthetic.
investigation_reports.initial_vitals: Before event: HR 88 bpm, BP 118/72 mmHg. After event: BP trends down and ischemic discomfort persists in the deterministic event timeline.
investigation_reports.not_supplied: Any test not explicitly listed is not ordered/not available; it must not be interpreted as normal.

history.chief_complaint: The patient initially presents with an acute coronary syndrome; during the simulated intervention, epicardial anatomy appears improved but myocardial perfusion remains poor.
history.history_of_present_illness: This is a complication branch attached to an ACS case, not a stand-alone diagnostic presentation.
relevant_history: Large thrombus burden in the fictional culprit lesion
medication_reconciliation: Periprocedural medication record is intentionally incomplete; learner must request reconciliation rather than infer doses
allergy_history: Contrast and medication allergy status must be explicitly checked before simulated intervention

pathway_review.label: Recognize poor tissue perfusion and activate the reviewed complication-response pathway
pathway_review.reason: Persistent ischemia despite apparent epicardial patency requires immediate attention in the scenario.

pathway_review.label: Declare success based only on an open-looking epicardial artery
pathway_review.reason: Ignores myocardial perfusion and clinical state.

pathway_review.label: Choose an unreviewed intervention without reassessing cause
pathway_review.reason: Complication management requires trained clinician judgment and case-specific review.

reference_findings.safety_review: Pause simulation, log event time, record hemodynamic changes, trigger team escalation, document the response and monitor for arrhythmia/shock. No drug doses or procedural maneuvers are provided.
reference_findings.simulated_clinical_course: Reference branch: complication is recognized, team response logged and perfusion improves in the simulated outcome; debrief highlights time to recognition and differential checks.
learning_objectives: Differentiate epicardial patency from tissue-level perfusion.
Use deterministic event timeline and escalation.
reference_findings.review_note: Synthetic scenario. Clinical values and pathway labels require qualified interventional cardiology review before deployment. Educational use only; not real-patient guidance.
